def: GST Identification Number. The 15-character ID of a registration: state code, PAN, entity number, 'Z' and a check character.
Goods and Services Tax Network. The government-owned company that runs the GST portal and its APIs.
Input tax credit. GST you paid on purchases that you can set off against GST you owe on sales.
Reverse charge mechanism. The buyer, not the seller, pays the GST to the government for notified supplies and imports of services.
Integrated GST. Charged on inter-state supplies and imports; collected by the Centre and shared with the destination state.
Central GST. The Centre's half of tax on an intra-state supply.
State GST. The state's half of tax on an intra-state supply.
Union Territory GST. Replaces SGST in UTs without a legislature, like Chandigarh or Ladakh.
Monthly or quarterly statement of outward supplies (sales), invoice by invoice for B2B.
Optional form to correct or add to a GSTR-1 for the same period, before filing that period's GSTR-3B.
A dynamic, constantly updating view of purchases as your suppliers report them.
A fixed monthly statement of ITC available to you, based on what suppliers filed by the cut-off. It's the basis for claiming ITC.
The monthly or quarterly summary return where you declare tax, claim ITC and actually pay.
Annual return for composition taxpayers.
Monthly return filed by an input service distributor, showing credit received and how it was passed to branches.
Return filed by government bodies that deduct GST TDS.
Return filed by e-commerce operators for GST TCS collected.
Annual return summarising the whole year's GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B.
Reconciliation statement between books and GSTR-9, for larger taxpayers.
Final return after a registration is cancelled.
Portal feature where you accept, reject or keep pending each supplier invoice before your GSTR-2B is finalised.
Quarterly Return Monthly Payment scheme for businesses up to ₹5 crore turnover: file quarterly, pay monthly.
Invoice Furnishing Facility. Lets QRMP taxpayers upload B2B invoices monthly so buyers get ITC sooner.
The challan form used to deposit GST into the electronic cash ledger.
Form to move money between heads within the electronic cash ledger.
Common Portal Identification Number. Generated when a challan is created.
Challan Identification Number. Generated by the bank once a challan is paid.
The summary of a show cause notice demanding tax.
Pre-notice intimation of tax the officer thinks is payable, before a formal show cause notice.
Intimation when GSTR-1 liability is higher than what was paid in GSTR-3B (rule 88C).
Intimation when ITC claimed in GSTR-3B is higher than GSTR-2B (rule 88D).
Form for voluntarily paying tax, interest or penalty, for example after spotting an error.
Summary of a demand order after adjudication.
Scrutiny notice pointing out discrepancies in returns.
The taxpayer's reply to an ASMT-10 scrutiny notice.
Notice of audit by the department under section 65.
Show cause notice for cancelling a registration.
Letter of Undertaking. Filed once a year so exports and SEZ supplies can be made without paying IGST.
Invoice Reference Number. A unique 64-character hash given to an e-invoice by the IRP.
Invoice Registration Portal. Validates and digitally signs e-invoices, and returns the IRN and QR code.
A B2B invoice registered on the IRP. Mandatory above a turnover threshold; without an IRN the invoice isn't valid.
Electronic document needed to move goods above ₹50,000 in value, with Part A (invoice details) and Part B (vehicle).
The vehicle or transport document section of an e-way bill.
Harmonized System of Nomenclature. The code that classifies goods, and decides the rate.
Services Accounting Code. Classification codes for services, starting with 99.
Special Economic Zone. Supplies to SEZ units are zero-rated, like exports.
An office that receives invoices for common services and distributes the ITC to branches in other states.
Online information database access and retrieval services, like streaming or cloud apps supplied from abroad.
Unique Identity Number, given to embassies and UN bodies to claim GST refunds.
Temporary Reference Number, used while completing a registration application.
Application Reference Number, the acknowledgement for a submitted application.
GST Practitioner. A professional enrolled to prepare and file returns on a taxpayer's behalf.
GST Suvidha Provider. Licensed by GSTN to connect software to the GST system's APIs.
Application Service Provider. Builds GST apps for taxpayers, usually connecting through a GSP.
Digital Signature Certificate. Required for companies and LLPs to file returns.
Electronic Verification Code. An OTP sent to the authorised signatory's mobile, used to file returns.
Aggregate annual turnover. All-India turnover of all registrations under a PAN, including exempt and export supplies. Drives most thresholds.
Business to business: a supply to a registered buyer who can claim ITC.
Business to consumer: a supply to an unregistered buyer.
GSTR-1 table for large inter-state B2C invoices (above ₹1 lakh).
GSTR-1 table for other B2C sales, reported in summary.
Credit and debit notes issued to registered persons (GSTR-1 Table 9B).
The state that gets the tax. It decides whether you charge IGST or CGST plus SGST.
A simplified scheme for small businesses: low flat tax on turnover, no ITC, no tax collected from customers.
Invoice without tax, issued by composition taxpayers or for exempt supplies.
Document reducing the value or tax of an earlier invoice, for returns, discounts or overcharging.
Document increasing the value or tax of an earlier invoice.
Supplies (exports, SEZ) taxed at effectively zero while keeping ITC, unlike exempt supplies.
A supply with no tax, where related ITC must be reversed. Includes nil-rated and non-taxable supplies.
Formal notice asking the taxpayer why tax, interest or penalty shouldn't be demanded.
The part of disputed tax (usually 10%) paid when filing an appeal, which stops recovery of the rest.
GST Appellate Tribunal, the second level of appeal after the Appellate Authority.
In GST, tax deducted at source by government bodies on payments to suppliers (2%).
In GST, tax collected at source by e-commerce operators on sellers' payouts.
E-commerce operator, a platform through which others sell goods or services.
Portal wallet holding money deposited by challan, plus TDS/TCS credits. Pays any liability.
Portal balance of ITC. Can pay output tax only, not interest or fees.
A fixed per-day charge for filing a return after its due date, separate from interest.
Registrations of the same PAN in different states. Supplies between them are taxable.
All-India turnover under a PAN, including exempt and export supplies, excluding taxes and inward RCM supplies.
List of activities treated as supplies even without consideration, like stock transfers.
List of activities that are neither goods nor services, like salaries and sale of land.
The deadline to claim ITC: 30 November after the financial year, or the annual return date if earlier.
The single demand section for FY 2024-25 onwards, replacing sections 73 and 74.
The signed code on an e-invoice with key details and the IRN, so anyone can verify it.
Return filed by a principal reporting goods sent to, moved between and received back from job workers.
